subject: Art & Design
title: The F-Pattern: How People Scan Web Pages
description: A short lesson to help you apply The F-Pattern: How People Scan Web Pages.

hook.text: Eye-tracking studies show people read web pages in an F shape. Top line, scan down-left, second line, then scroll.

buildup.text: The F-pattern was discovered by Jakob Nielsen using heat maps of 232 users reading thousands of pages.

discovery.text: Users barely read. They scan headlines, first sentences, and bold text. The rest is skimmed or ignored entirely.

twist.text: Placing key content in the bottom-right is like hiding it. Almost nobody's eyes reach there naturally.

climax.text: Effective web design puts the most critical information top-left and uses headings to catch scanning eyes.

punchline.text: Don't design for readers. Design for scanners.

quiz.question: What does the F-pattern describe in web design?
options: The way users scan pages — horizontally at top, then down the left side
A color scheme for financial websites

details.summary: Eye-tracking studies reveal that users scan web pages in an F-shaped pattern — reading the first line fully, scanning part of the second line, then scrolling down the left edge. This pattern means content placed in the top-left and along the left column gets the most attention.
details.whyItMatters: The F-pattern proves that users don't read web pages — they scan them. Designers who understand this pattern place critical information where eyes actually land rather than where they hope users will look.
takeaways: Users scan web pages in an F-shaped pattern, not linearly
The first line and left edge receive the most attention
Critical information must be placed where eyes actually land

faq.question: Does the F-pattern apply to all cultures?
faq.answer: The F-pattern applies to left-to-right reading cultures. Right-to-left languages (Arabic, Hebrew) show a mirrored pattern. The principle is universal — users scan rather than read — but the direction depends on writing system.

faq.question: How do you design for the F-pattern?
faq.answer: Place the most important content in the first two paragraphs. Start paragraphs and list items with informative keywords. Use subheadings, bullet points, and bold text to create scannable content. Left-align important elements. Avoid uniform text blocks that the eye skips during scanning.
